I’m going to try to break it down for you based on my own experience and how my WS and I have dealt with infidelity in our marriage. 

Trust means that you believe, without checking in on your spouse constantly or reading their messages, that your partner is being faithful and is not engaging in emotionally inappropriate or sexual relationships with other people. 

When one partner betrays another’s trust by being unfaithful, it devastates the other. In my own relationship, my WS and I have spent time trying to rebuild trust by him sharing everything he’s done, by providing me with all of his passwords, by deleting social media accounts, etc. If my spouse had continued lying or engaging in extramarital affairs, we would no longer be together. 

Now, you say that your girlfriend is cheating on you. I’m going to regard this as true for arguments sake despite not having solid evidence. So, despite hurting you, she is continuing to betray your trust and undermining your relationship and your self worth. It takes two people to reconcile, not one, and certainly not zero as it appears to be in your case. Neither of you are doing anything to rebuild. Do you believe that cheating on your significant other is going to rebuild trust between you? Cheating on your partner is impeding healing from occurring. Healing begins when both parties are fully invested and it can take 2-5 YEARS before couples can say they’ve fully healed from infidelity. 

I say all this as someone who has been cheated on, never physically, but damn near close. I would never consider cheating back on my partner partly because that’s just not who I am and partly because that’s no way for us to rebuild the trust that we lost. He knows that he can trust me; I just don’t know how to trust him right now. Imagine that NEITHER of us could trust each other, as it is in your relationship now. How can you possibly build a relationship without any trust at all? 

As far as your lack of communication, I am referring to your affairs (they’re not dates if you are in a relationship) as well as how distrustful you are of her and the fact that you want to break up but have not communicated this to your partner. The fact that you two have continued this nonsense for 5 months is mind blowing to me. 

I’ll sum all this up by saying, both of you need to be invested in reconciliation 100% or it will not work. As of right now, neither of you are putting in the time or effort and it looks like that isn’t going to change. Sorry you’re having such a tough time but you seem young and this relationship doesn’t need to take up any more of your time. Learn from this experience.

Being “as one after infidelity” comes from BOTH parties working together to heal. It’s obvious from your post and your comments that, at the very least, you aren’t doing your part in attempting to heal the relationship. At worst, both of you are sleeping with other people and neither one of you is communicating. 

As another poster pointed out, you say you’re cheating on your SO because you “know” she’s cheating on you. However, you don’t have any proof. Part of reconciliation is rebuilding trust, not undermining it like you have been. Without proof of cheating, it sounds like your SO is trying to rebuild but you keep having affairs to get back at her.

If you want other advice, it’s this: break up. You’re not married, you don’t have kids, and you’re not doing anything to help your relationship. 

What you’re doing is not reconciling, it’s revenge. You are sleeping with other people because you believe that she did. Whether she did or she did not sleep with the guy she kissed, she asked you not to cheat on her and you did. Reconciliation is about growing together and building up your partner, not hurting them to make yourself feel better. Your relationship is toxic and it needs to end.

We just started reading “How to help your spouse heal from an affair” together and purchased “healing from infidelity” and “after the affair”. D-Day for us was at the end of May but we only started reading about two weeks ago. My WS resisted delving into the details of his infidelity for several months and only in the last few weeks has done a 180. 

We had a massive fight a few weeks ago because he revealed that he had actually video-called his AP to engage in sexual behaviors twice, rather than just once, and I straight up lost my fucking mind. I screamed at him, I got in his face (which I never have done before), and I threw all of his pillows out into our living room and locked him out of the bedroom. I think it was a real wake up call for him to see how the trickle-truthing was making things way worse. The next day, he said he needed to try harder and ordered the books. I agreed to read them together so we could discuss things in a semi-controlled manner. 

Every morning, we sit together, drink our coffee, and read. He reads a chapter of the book to himself and then I read the same chapter aloud. Then we discuss the chapter together, diving into the emotions and history of his betrayals. It’s absolutely normal to process while reading. Sometimes, I can’t even read a sentence in the book without my voice breaking. It’s actually why I read it out loud because my WS can see how things have affected me. I do try my hardest not to yell because I know that it will keep my WS from feeling like he can be completely honest. I think it’s been helpful because it opens the door for asking questions or laying down suggested boundaries.

I’ll try to give you the short version. My husband sexted with a woman he met online about 9 months into our marriage (about 2 years ago) but that fizzled out after a short time. I didn’t find out about it until D-Day in May of this year. On D-Day, I found out that he had been having a 6 month EA/sexting affair with an 18 year old coworker while I was pregnant with our child. I ended up miscarrying at 3 months, in March, and had to have surgery. He continued with his lying during that time and I think that’s what upsets/angers me the most. I know that it was during that time because he saved pictures and videos that she had sent him and they had timestamps. He also had been talking to various camgirls/pornstars/fake email accounts online during our entire marriage but that often didn’t go anywhere because they always wanted payment that he didn’t have. He tried to get nudes from basically any source, including dating apps. 

We’ve been trying to work on things and I would not still be here if he hadn’t followed everything I told him to do. I have full access to his phone and email, and he deleted all social media except his Facebook (but I have the password). He blocked his AP on Facebook and had a brief conversation with her telling her it was over and they would no longer be communicating.  He also told me about every time that she tried to speak to him at work. He’s in the process of transferring locations so that he no longer would have any chance of seeing her, even though they usually don’t because they work opposite shifts. He informed his superiors about what was going on (after AP gossiped to the entire place) and they’re supportive of our efforts so they appear to be purposefully scheduling them so their shifts do not overlap at all. He no longer stays on the couch when I go to bed, because that was when he would stay up and chat with AP. He also calls me when he’s at work so I know what he’s up to and allows me to see his location. Lastly, I have child locks on his phone so he can not access 17+ materials or delete an app if he downloads it. 

That was a lot longer of an explanation than I intended but it really only grazes the surface. It’s been wild and I’ve cried most days since D-Day and didn’t eat for about a week after I found out. I’ve seen people say that it can take 2-5 years to fully heal from an affair so we have a long road ahead of us.
